name: gate-driver-core-drive-postlayout
description: Post-layout re-run of gate-driver-core-drive (issue #105, T1 checklist item 7): same end-to-end stimulus chain -- logic-in (IN) -> level_shifter -> output_stage -> 1 nF reference load -- but against the LVS-extracted netlist of layout/gate_driver_core.gds rather than design/netlist/gate_driver_core.spice. The manifest DUT (layout/lvs/gate_driver_core.extracted.spice) is the device-level extraction with parallel-identical fingers folded back to m=<n>, plus the 4 XCCOMP* MiM series capacitors (#166, never folded): drawn W/L, measured junction AS/AD/PS/PD and extracted drain/gate/source connectivity, no interconnect parasitics. The RC-annotated variant (layout/lvs/gate_driver_core.extracted-rc.spice, klt extract --parasitics: 959 discrete fingers + the 4 XCCOMP* caps + 2885 R / 20 C, including both ground rails' own per-terminal legs -- each rebound to that leg's own device's rail, since the deck reports the two grounds as one merged net -- but still no net-to-net coupling) gets its own full-grid record, run with --dut; the two answer different questions -- whether the drawn geometry realises the schematic's devices, and what the drawn wires cost. See layout/lvs/mk_extracted_dut.py's module docstring for exactly what each DUT measures vs. back-annotates vs. does not model at all (net-to-net coupling capacitance).
analyses: meas tran trise10_90 TRIG v(OUT) VAL=outlo RISE=1 TARG v(OUT) VAL=outhi RISE=1
meas tran tfall10_90 TRIG v(OUT) VAL=outhi FALL=1 TARG v(OUT) VAL=outlo FALL=1
meas tran tpdlh TRIG v(IN) VAL=inmid RISE=1 TARG v(OUT) VAL=outmid RISE=1
meas tran tpdhl TRIG v(IN) VAL=inmid FALL=1 TARG v(OUT) VAL=outmid FALL=1

trise_s.description: spec Sec.3: 10-90% rise into 1nF reference load < 50ns, end-to-end IN->OUT (no stretch target -- spec Sec.3's Rise/fall row is '-' at the 6V stretch corner)

tfall_s.description: spec Sec.3: 10-90% fall into 1nF reference load < 50ns, end-to-end IN->OUT (no stretch target -- spec Sec.3's Rise/fall row is '-' at the 6V stretch corner)

tpdlh_s.description: spec Sec.3: end-to-end low-to-high propagation delay < 50ns nominal, < 25ns at the 6V vdrv stretch corner. Evaluated per corner tier via the harness's stretch override (#147/#125); this is the row post-layout interconnect RC moves most

tpdhl_s.description: spec Sec.3: end-to-end high-to-low propagation delay < 50ns nominal, < 25ns at the 6V vdrv stretch corner

ipeak_source_a.description: spec Sec.3: peak source current into 1nF load >= 0.5A nominal, >= 1A at the 6V vdrv stretch corner

ipeak_sink_a.description: spec Sec.3: peak sink current into 1nF load >= 0.5A nominal, >= 1A at the 6V vdrv stretch corner

vout_max_v.description: sanity: OUT must not exceed the swept drive rail plus headroom

vout_min_v.description: sanity: OUT must not undershoot below GND_DRV -- inherited band, see sibling record

indrv_max_v.description: spec Sec.2.3 gate-ceiling evidence: IN_DRV, the level shifter's drive-rail-referenced output and the thick-oxide gate of the output stage's first taper inverter -- a real top-level net on both the schematic and the extracted netlist

indrv_min_v.description: sanity: IN_DRV must not undershoot GND_DRV -- inherited band, see sibling record

n1_max_v.description: spec Sec.2.3 gate-ceiling evidence: output-stage taper node n1 (x2_n1 -- flat post-extraction net name for the schematic-side x2.n1, gate of MP2/MN2)

n1_min_v.description: sanity: taper node n1 must not undershoot GND_DRV -- inherited band, see sibling record
